summary: A commercial three-act shape in fifteen beats: a hero, a choice that opens a new world, a midpoint that raises the stakes, a lowest point, and a finale that answers the opening.
_lineage: A widely taught commercial structure, best known from a 2005 screenwriting book by Blake Snyder and its 2018 adaptation for novelists. The beat names and descriptions here are our own; _commonNames records the names writers usually use, for recognition only.

beats.name: Opening image
beats.describe: A snapshot of the hero's life before anything changes: the 'before' picture that the ending will answer.
lookFor: the hero in their usual routine
a flaw or lack shown, not explained

beats.name: Theme hinted
beats.describe: Someone says or shows, often in passing, what the story is really about. The hero does not understand it yet.
lookFor: a line of advice or a warning the hero shrugs off

beats.name: Setup
beats.describe: The hero's world, what they want, what is wrong in their life, and the people who will matter.
lookFor: home, work and the people around the hero
small problems that will need fixing

beats.name: Catalyst
beats.describe: The event that ends the old normal: news, a loss, an invitation, an attack. It happens to the hero.
lookFor: a message, death, offer or arrival that cannot be ignored

beats.name: Debate
beats.describe: The hero resists, weighs the cost or prepares. Whether to go is asked out loud or in action.
lookFor: hesitation, argument or preparation before a commitment

beats.name: Into the new world
beats.describe: The hero chooses, and steps into an upside-down version of their life. The choice is theirs, not forced on them.
lookFor: a departure, an oath, a door closing behind them

beats.name: Second story
beats.describe: A new relationship (a love, a friend, a mentor, a rival) that carries the theme and will help the hero answer it.
lookFor: a new person the hero keeps returning to

beats.name: The premise in play
beats.describe: The part readers came for: the hero testing the new world, winning or failing at it. The promise of the cover is delivered here.
lookFor: set pieces that could only happen in this story's world

beats.name: Midpoint
beats.describe: A false victory or a false defeat that raises the stakes. A clock may start, a truth may come out, the fun ends.
lookFor: a win that costs more than it looks
a reveal that changes the goal

beats.name: Pressure closes in
beats.describe: Enemies regroup outside; doubt, jealousy and the hero's own flaw work from inside. The team frays.
lookFor: setbacks that come from the hero's own choices
allies pulling apart

beats.name: Lowest point
beats.describe: Everything seems lost. Something or someone dies, literally or as a hope, and the old way of thinking dies with it.
lookFor: a death, a betrayal or a failure that looks final

beats.name: Dark night
beats.describe: The hero sits with the loss. This is the darkest moment, just before the realisation.
lookFor: grief, despair or stillness after the loss

beats.name: The answer
beats.describe: The second story and the theme come together: the hero sees what to do, and chooses again, differently.
lookFor: a realisation that uses what the second story taught

beats.name: Finale
beats.describe: The hero acts on the answer and applies what they learned. The old world is changed or saved, and the flaw is gone.
lookFor: a plan carried out under pressure
the hero doing what they could not do at the start

beats.name: Closing image
beats.describe: The 'after' picture, the mirror of the opening image, showing how much has changed.
lookFor: the opening situation revisited, transformed
